residual_risks: Commit holds admitMu across `b.in <- request{...}` (batcher.go Commit). If b.in is full (Size items queued) while commitLoop is inside a long user commit fn, that Commit blocks holding the mutex, so a signal-driven Shutdown blocks on admitMu.Lock() until the loop drains. Before the change Shutdown's own `b.in <- quit` would have blocked the same way on a full channel, so this is not a regression. The send also ignores ctx (pre-existing), so a cancelled ctx cannot unblock the wait. No re-entry into Commit/Shutdown exists from the commit fns (dropbox commitBatch, googlephotos commitBatch), so no deadlock cycle was found.

fs.Debugf(b.f, ...) in Commit now runs under admitMu, so a slow or blocked log sink or slow Fs.String() would stall Shutdown and all other Commits. The test's blockingStringer deliberately exploits this. Production Fs.String() is trivial, so the impact is theoretical.

Test timing: on unfixed code the test only reproduces the bug if the Shutdown goroutine closes b.closed within the 100ms window before blocker.release is closed. Under heavy CI load it could pass without exercising the race (false green, not flaky red). It mutates the global fs config LogLevel (ci.LogLevel) without synchronization, which is safe here only because the tests are sequential and channel handoffs order the reads and writes.
